acceptance.given: The repository Toolchain route policy is evaluated against the supported package set.

oracle.expected: The VDD package route is present and accessible through the supported shared replay capability.
forbidden: Supported VDD package routes are unavailable or removed.
oracle.observable: The supported-route evaluation and the VDD route's accessible replay entry.

acceptance.then: The supported VDD package route remains available.
acceptance.when: The supported route set is exposed or changed.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Remove the supported VDD route from route resolution and require the behavior test to fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Preserve the VDD package route as an accessible irreducible supported Toolchain route.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: The supported route set remains backward-compatible and cannot remove the VDD route.

slice_hint.state_transition: The pre-change supported-route baseline retains an accessible VDD package route after route-set evaluation.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The route selector resolves the VDD package route through the shared capability and rejects its removal or unavailability.

acceptance.given: A Toolchain external-process request is ready for execution with configured finite time and output limits.

oracle.expected: The execution record reaches a deterministic terminal state within its configured finite time and output limits; exhaustion is unsuccessful.
forbidden: An external process runs without a finite time bound.
Budget exhaustion is treated as successful.
oracle.observable: The process-executor result exposes its configured bounds and terminal outcome during the external-process execution check.

acceptance.then: The Toolchain stops or completes the external process within the configured finite bound and records an unsuccessful deterministic terminal outcome on exhaustion.
acceptance.when: During the NFR-7 external-process validation invocation.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Exercise process_executor_v2 with a process that exceeds its configured finite timeout and require an unsuccessful bounded terminal result.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce finite time and output limits for each Toolchain external process and classify exhaustion as an unsuccessful deterministic terminal state.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persistent state or schema migration; reverting restores the prior process-execution behavior.

slice_hint.state_transition: external-process executing -> completed or stopped within finite bound -> deterministic successful or unsuccessful terminal state
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Each external process has a finite time/output bound and exhaustion terminates unsuccessfully without reducing coverage.

acceptance.given: A source-supported existing Stable Package is selected for a Matrix run using the repository replay implementation and its bound stable/candidate matrix inputs.

oracle.expected: The validator emits Stable-package eligibility evidence containing a verifiable provenance reference for the source-supported existing behavior and an immutable package identity bound before any Matrix execution begins.
forbidden: Eligibility is accepted when the provenance reference is missing, unverifiable, or not tied to source-supported existing behavior.
Eligibility is accepted when the Stable Package identity is absent, mutable, or first bound after execution starts.
oracle.observable: A machine-readable Stable-package eligibility record is inspected for provenance reference validity, immutable identity, and a pre-run binding marker, with the record linked to the selected package identity and Matrix run.

acceptance.then: The Stable Package is eligible only when both source-supported provenance and the pre-run immutable identity are independently evidenced.
acceptance.when: During the Toolchain replay evaluation phase, before Matrix Case execution is launched.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Mutate or remove the Stable Package provenance reference while keeping the remaining Matrix inputs unchanged; the eligibility validator must reject the package.
Provide Stable eligibility evidence whose immutable identity is missing, mutable, or timestamped after Matrix execution; the validator must reject eligibility.

affected_subjects: Stable Package eligibility validation and pre-run identity binding
slice_hint.behavior_change: Make Stable Package eligibility evidence require a verifiable source-supported provenance reference and an immutable identity that is bound before Matrix execution; reject missing, unverifiable, late, or mutable bindings.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing replay and Matrix result schemas; rollback restores prior Stable eligibility behavior while retaining fail-closed rejection for missing provenance or pre-run identity.

slice_hint.state_transition: Unestablished Stable eligibility -> provenance and immutable identity validated and bound before run -> Stable Package eligible; any missing or late binding -> ineligible terminal state.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Stable eligibility passes only when the evidence record proves source-supported provenance and an immutable package identity bound before Matrix execution; otherwise the terminal result is unsuccessful.

acceptance.given: The compiled obligation graph contains Atomic Obligation-to-selector mappings to evaluate.

oracle.expected: Exact-cover validation reports that every Atomic Obligation has selector coverage and every selector node maps back to its covered Atomic Obligation.
forbidden: An Atomic Obligation is covered by selectors without reverse coverage.
A selector node is linked without corresponding Atomic Obligation coverage.
oracle.observable: The Exact Cover validator's graph-validation result for selector relationships, evaluated when the graph is compiled or exact-cover validation runs.

acceptance.then: The validation result establishes forward and reverse Exact Cover for every Atomic Obligation-to-selector relationship.
acceptance.when: When the obligation graph is compiled or the Exact Cover validator evaluates selector coverage.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the exact-cover negative validator against a selector mapping with an omitted reverse Atomic Obligation relation and require graph validation to fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Validate selector coverage as bidirectional Exact Cover: each Atomic Obligation maps to selector coverage and each selector maps back to its covered Atomic Obligation.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persistent state or schema migration; reverting restores prior Exact Cover validation behavior.

slice_hint.state_transition: unverified selector mapping -> bidirectional selector Exact Cover evaluation -> validated or deterministic violation result
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The compiled graph has no forward-only selector coverage and no selector node without reverse Atomic Obligation coverage.
